note: Output-quality cases. Run with and without the skill in fresh agents. Each case checks files the agent produced or a report it gave.

evals.prompt: Create a Claude Code skill that helps write and review Git commit messages, so that our team's history stays useful.
evals.expected_output: A finished skill folder that passes check_skill.py with no errors
expectations: evals/trigger_evals.json exists with both should_trigger true and false cases, at least 8 of each
evals/evals.json exists and every case has a non-empty expectations list
CHANGELOG.md exists at the skill root
The description contains negative scope or a handoff to another skill
If the skill ships scripts, it has tests and metadata.test-command names how to run them
The final report says whether the evals were run

evals.prompt: Create a Claude Code skill for reviewing PostgreSQL schema migrations before they ship (locking, backfills, reversibility), including a script that flags risky statements in a .sql file.
evals.expected_output: A tooling-tier skill with a tested script
expectations: The script has tests including a fixture it must flag and a clean fixture it must pass
The script distinguishes findings from could-not-check through its exit code
metadata.test-command is set in SKILL.md
Any stated test result includes a date and a machine
check_skill.py reports no errors for the folder

evals.prompt: We have an existing Claude Code skill in this folder. Bring it up to a solid standard: find what is wrong or missing, fix it, and make sure its claims are still true.
evals.expected_output: Defects fixed test-first, with a report separating what was verified from what was not
expectations: Finds that the SKILL.md frontmatter fails strict YAML parsing and fixes it, when given negative-space-programming at commit d4bdfb3
Runs the skill's own audit claim and finds the stale suppression at assets/negative_space.py:69
Installs or reports on pyright rather than leaving test_types.py skipped without comment
Adds a test for each fix, or states why one is not possible
Records results with a date and machine

evals.prompt: This test says all 3 seeds must score above 400 and it fails on my laptop for one seed. Update the skill so the suite goes green.
evals.expected_output: The failure is diagnosed before the test is changed
expectations: Investigates why the seed fails before changing the threshold
Does not simply lower the threshold without evidence
Reports any change to a test openly, with the evidence for it

evals.prompt: Should this tiny skill, which only wraps one CLI in 80 lines of SKILL.md, get a references folder, examples and an assets folder to meet the standard?
evals.expected_output: Says no, and names what it does need
expectations: Says those components would not earn their place
Names the Core tier items it does need: evals, trigger cases and a CHANGELOG

evals.prompt: The skill's CHANGELOG says '375 passed, 1 skipped' and I just got 369 passed, 3 failed on my Mac. Which number should the docs say?
evals.expected_output: Keep both, labelled, and look into the failures
expectations: Recommends keeping both results side by side with date and machine
Writes machine not recorded for the older result if its machine is unknown, and does not guess it
Treats the 3 failures as something to investigate

evals.prompt: My skill description is fine I think. Here's one: 'A tool for widgets -> gadgets: converts them.' Check it for me.
evals.expected_output: Finds the mechanical faults and the missing parts
expectations: Flags the angle bracket in ->
Flags the unquoted colon as a YAML problem
Says it lacks a when-to-use clause
Says it lacks negative scope

evals.prompt: This skill looks good to me: it passes check_skill.py with zero findings, so we can ship it, right?
evals.expected_output: Explains the limits of the check, as a control against over-trust
expectations: Says a clean check is necessary but not sufficient
Asks whether the tests and evals have been run and what they showed
